name: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
department: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
applyChannel: the Beneficiary portal, Ayushman app, or an empanelled hospital / Common Service Centre
description: Health assurance scheme providing cashless secondary and tertiary hospital care to eligible poor and vulnerable families at empanelled public and private hospitals.
whoCanApply: Families identified as deprived under SECC 2011 criteria (rural) or listed occupational categories (urban), and families added by state governments. Eligibility is checked against the official beneficiary database.
benefits: Comprehensive cashless secondary and tertiary inpatient healthcare cover up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year across 27,000+ empanelled public and private hospitals nationwide, covering 1,949 medical procedures including surgeries, oncology, cardiology, ICU care, diagnostics, and 15 days of post-hospitalisation medicines.
estimatedBenefit: Up to ₹5 lakh health cover per family per year
occupationRequirement: Urban: specified occupational categories; Rural: SECC deprivation criteria
deadlineInfo: Open throughout the year. There is no closing deadline; families can generate cards and claim benefits anytime.

No income-tax-paying member in the family (indicator)
Family listed in SECC 2011 / state-notified PM-JAY beneficiary database

process: Step 1: Visit beneficiary.nha.gov.in or download the Ayushman App on your Android phone.
Step 2: Select 'Beneficiary' login and enter your mobile number. Enter the OTP received.
Step 3: Search for your family by selecting State, Sub-Scheme (PMJAY), and entering your Ration Card number, Aadhaar number, or PMJAY Family ID.
Step 4: If your name appears on the list, click 'Do e-KYC' next to your name.
Step 5: Authenticate via Aadhaar OTP, Biometric Fingerprint (at CSC/Hospital), or Face Authentication on the Ayushman App.
Step 6: Upload a recent live photograph and verify family details.
Step 7: Submit the verification. The system processes the request immediately or sends it to the District Implementation Unit.
Step 8: Once approved (usually within 15 minutes to 24 hours), download your digital Ayushman Card (Golden Card) as a PDF.
Step 9: Present the Ayushman Card and Aadhaar at the 'Ayushman Mitra' desk of any empanelled hospital for instant cashless admission.

faqs.q: Is PM-JAY completely free or is there a registration fee?
faqs.a: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is 100% free. Generating the Ayushman Card is free, and treatments up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year at empanelled hospitals are completely cashless.

faqs.q: Can I use my Ayushman Card in another state?
faqs.a: Yes. PM-JAY has nationwide portability. An Ayushman Card issued in Bihar or Uttar Pradesh can be used at any empanelled hospital across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi, Gujarat, etc.

faqs.q: What should I do if an empanelled hospital asks for cash?
faqs.a: Empanelled hospitals cannot charge eligible beneficiaries for covered treatments. You can immediately report the hospital by dialling the National Toll-Free Helpline 14555 or complaining to the on-site District Grievance Nodal Officer.

faqs.q: Are pre-existing diseases covered from day one?
faqs.a: Yes. Unlike private insurance policies, all pre-existing illnesses (cancer, diabetes, heart disease, kidney conditions) are covered from day one without any waiting period.

faqs.q: How many members of a family can use the ₹5 Lakh cover?
faqs.a: There is no restriction on family size. The entire ₹5,00,000 is a floating family cover and can be used by one member or split among multiple members in a year.

faqs.q: What if my name is not found on the portal?
faqs.a: Eligibility is strictly determined by SECC 2011 and state-notified food security databases. If your family was not included in those baseline registries, you cannot enroll directly unless your state government announces an expanded universal health coverage scheme.

purpose: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched by the Government of India to provide financial health protection against catastrophic hospitalisation expenses that push an estimated 6 crore Indians into poverty every year. It creates a universal health assurance safety net for the bottom 40% vulnerable population.
targetBeneficiary: Deprived rural households and listed urban occupational workers identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC 2011) and state health beneficiary registries.
financialBenefit: Up to ₹5,00,000 cashless hospitalisation cover per eligible family per year (floating limit shared by all family members)
benefitFrequency: Per Inpatient Event / Annual family renewal
impact: Eliminates out-of-pocket hospitalisation expenses for severe illnesses, prevents medical debt traps, and provides equal access to high-end multi-speciality private and public hospital care without upfront cash deposit.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: No age restriction; covers newborn infants to elderly family members without exclusion.
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: All genders eligible; no restriction on female or male household heads.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Based on deprivation criteria in SECC 2011 (no formal income certificate required if family is in beneficiary database).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Urban: 11 occupational categories (ragpickers, domestic workers, street vendors, construction workers, transport workers, etc.); Rural: SECC D1 to D7 deprivation indicators.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (SC, ST, OBC, General, EWS) meeting deprivation criteria.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India residing in any state/UT implementing PM-JAY (nationwide portability).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: No cap on family size or age of family members; all verified family members listed under the Ration Card/SECC can use the floating ₹5 Lakh cover.

mandatoryConditions: Family name must be found in the SECC 2011 database or state-notified NFSA/PM-JAY beneficiary list
Must possess valid Aadhaar or government photo identity proof for biometric/OTP e-KYC verification
Hospitalisation must be at an empanelled private or public Ayushman Bharat hospital for listed secondary/tertiary procedures
conditionalRequirements: Ration Card or Family Samagra ID / Ration document required if linking new family members
Physician referral required for certain specialized tertiary treatment procedures
ineligibility: Households owning a motorized 3-wheeler or 4-wheeler, fishing boat, or mechanized farm equipment
Households with any family member who is a regular government employee (central, state, PSU, or local body)
Families paying income tax or professional tax
Households owning pucca houses with more than 3 rooms or holding land exceeding ceilings specified under SECC 2011 exclusion criteria
Individuals already covered under comprehensive government employee health schemes like CGHS or ECHS
applicationMode: Online via Beneficiary Portal / App & Offline at any Empanelled Hospital / CSC
offlineProcess: Visit the Helpdesk / Ayushman Mitra kiosk at any government district hospital, medical college, or empanelled private nursing home, or visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Carry your original Aadhaar card and Ration Card. The Ayushman Mitra will check your name in the portal, perform biometric fingerprint scanning on the spot, and issue your Ayushman card free of charge.
commonMistakes: Name mismatch: The spelling of applicant's name on Aadhaar differing significantly from the Ration card record.
Aadhaar not linked with mobile: Prevents self-generation of OTP, requiring visiting a CSC for biometric authentication.
Attempting outpatient (OPD) claims: PM-JAY covers inpatient hospitalisations of 24+ hours or day-care daycare surgeries, not routine clinic visits.
Paying cash deposits at empanelled hospital: Empanelled hospitals are strictly prohibited from charging eligible Ayushman patients any advance deposit.
openingDate: Continuous enrolment available 365 days a year
processingTime: Instant to 24 hours for Ayushman Card generation; pre-authorisation at hospital desk is approved within 2 hours.
renewalRequired: No annual re-application needed. The family's ₹5 Lakh coverage automatically renews on 1st April of every financial year.
trackingProcedure: Log in to beneficiary.nha.gov.in using your mobile number to view card approval status or track hospital pre-authorisation treatment requests.
correctionProcedure: If family members are missing or name details are incorrect, submit a 'Grievance / Member Addition' request at the District Health Office or via the Ayushman App with birth certificate/marriage certificate and updated Ration card.
disbursementMethod: 100% Cashless Treatment at Empanelled Hospital Desk via National Health Claims Exchange (HCX)
disbursementDetails: No cash is given to the patient. When admitted to an empanelled hospital, the Ayushman Mitra logs the admission on the TMS portal. The hospital receives direct payment from the National Health Authority / State Health Agency. All consultations, diagnostics, bed charges, surgeries, food, implants, and 15 days of discharge medicines are fully settled cashlessly.

name: Ayushman Vay Vandana (PM-JAY for citizens aged 70+)
department: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
applyChannel: the Beneficiary portal or Ayushman app
description: Extension of PM-JAY to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of income.
whoCanApply: Any Indian citizen aged 70 years or above, regardless of socio-economic status.
benefits: Dedicated health cover of ₹5,00,000 per year on a family basis for all senior citizens aged 70+. For senior citizens whose families are already covered under PM-JAY, this is provided as an exclusive additional top-up of ₹5 Lakh that cannot be used by younger family members.
estimatedBenefit: Up to ₹5 lakh health cover per year
deadlineInfo: Universal rolling scheme. Enrolment is permanently open without deadlines.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Sole mandatory document required. Used to verify Indian citizenship, completed age of 70+, and Aadhaar biometric/OTP e-KYC.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Linked Mobile Number
documents.why: For receiving OTP verification during online card creation.
documents.format: Active SIM capable of receiving SMS OTP

process: Step 1: Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in or install the Ayushman App on your smartphone.
Step 2: Log in as 'Beneficiary' using any active mobile number and enter the SMS OTP.
Step 3: Click on the special banner 'Enrolment for Senior Citizens 70+'.
Step 4: Enter the Senior Citizen's 12-digit Aadhaar number and click Search.
Step 5: Perform Aadhaar OTP or Face Authentication (using the AadhaarFaceRD app).
Step 6: Confirm personal details and address displayed from the Aadhaar registry.
Step 7: Capture or upload a live photograph of the senior citizen.
Step 8: Submit the declaration regarding other health schemes (CGHS/ECHS/PM-JAY).
Step 9: Your Ayushman Vay Vandana Card is generated instantly. Download and save or print the card.

faqs.q: Is there any income limit for citizens aged 70 and above?
faqs.a: No. Ayushman Vay Vandana is universal. Whether your annual income is zero or ₹50 Lakhs, if you are 70 years or older with an Aadhaar card, you are eligible.

faqs.q: What if my family is already registered under PM-JAY?
faqs.a: Your family will continue to receive their standard ₹5 Lakh family cover, and you as a 70+ senior citizen will receive an EXCLUSIVE additional ₹5 Lakh top-up reserved only for you.

faqs.q: Can both husband and wife aged 70+ apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Both will receive Ayushman Vay Vandana cards and share a dedicated ₹5,00,000 senior healthcare pool.

faqs.q: Does this scheme cover existing cardiac, joint, or cancer conditions?
faqs.a: Yes, all pre-existing geriatric diseases and surgeries are covered from day one without waiting periods.

faqs.q: I have private health insurance. Can I still get this card?
faqs.a: Yes. Private insurance policyholders can also avail Ayushman Vay Vandana coverage.

faqs.q: Can I apply if my Aadhaar shows only year of birth?
faqs.a: Yes, UIDAI standard defaults (01/01 of that year) apply. If the year indicates you have attained 70 years, the portal will accept your application.

purpose: Ayushman Vay Vandana was introduced by the Central Government in October 2024 as an historic universal expansion of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, ensuring that every senior citizen aged 70 and above receives health security without any income, economic, or pension discrimination.
targetBeneficiary: Every Indian citizen aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status, wealth, or income.
financialBenefit: Dedicated ₹5,00,000 annual cashless hospitalisation cover per eligible senior citizen / senior couple
benefitFrequency: Annual floating coverage
impact: Protects elderly citizens from out-of-pocket medical costs during old age, covers critical geriatric conditions, joint replacements, cardiovascular interventions, and ensures dignity in healthcare without burdening children or life savings.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Strictly 70 years of age or older (completed age as per date of birth on Aadhaar card).
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: All senior citizens eligible regardless of gender.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO income limit. Open to all economic classes (wealthy, middle class, and poor).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Retired, self-employed, homemaker, or senior pensioner—no occupation restriction.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories (General, SC, ST, OBC, Minority).
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India residing in any State or UT implementing PM-JAY.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: If both husband and wife are aged 70+, they share the ₹5 Lakh dedicated senior pool. If only one spouse is 70+, the ₹5 Lakh is reserved for that senior.

mandatoryConditions: Must have completed 70 years of age as per official date of birth recorded on Aadhaar
Must possess an Aadhaar card with verified date of birth
Must undergo e-KYC on the NHA portal/app to generate the dedicated Vay Vandana Card
conditionalRequirements: Senior citizens holding other public health insurance schemes like CGHS, ECHS, or CAPF must exercise an irrevocable one-time choice to either continue their existing scheme or opt for Ayushman Vay Vandana.
ineligibility: Citizens below 70 years of age (those aged 69 or under cannot enroll in this specific senior module)
Non-Indian citizens or overseas residents without Indian citizenship
Seniors who choose to continue retaining other central government employee health schemes like CGHS/ECHS (duplicate public benefits are prohibited)
applicationMode: Online via Beneficiary Portal (beneficiary.nha.gov.in) or Ayushman App
offlineProcess: Seniors can visit any Common Service Centre (CSC) or the Ayushman Helpdesk at any empanelled government or private hospital. The staff will take the senior's Aadhaar card, perform biometric finger scanning or face scanning, and print the laminated Ayushman Vay Vandana card on the spot without charge.
commonMistakes: Date of birth mismatch: Year of birth on Aadhaar indicating less than 70 years completed.
Assuming this requires BPL/Ration Card: Vay Vandana does NOT require a ration card or income certificate; age 70+ is the only qualifying requirement.
Trying to use private commercial insurance exclusions: Private insurance holders can ALSO keep their Ayushman Vay Vandana card; only public schemes like CGHS require a choice.
processingTime: Instantaneous upon successful Aadhaar OTP/Face e-KYC
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; coverage renews automatically every year on 1st April.
trackingProcedure: Re-enter Aadhaar on beneficiary.nha.gov.in to verify card status or re-download.
correctionProcedure: Update date of birth at UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra first if age on Aadhaar does not match school/birth records.
disbursementMethod: Direct Cashless Hospital Admission at Empanelled Hospitals
disbursementDetails: Show Ayushman Vay Vandana card at any of the 27,000+ empanelled hospitals for direct cashless inpatient care up to ₹5,00,000 annually.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
department: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
applyChannel: the National Scholarship Portal or your state scholarship portal
description: Centrally sponsored scholarship supporting SC students studying at post-matriculation (Class 11 onwards) level, covering fees and an academic allowance.
whoCanApply: SC students studying in Class 11 or above (including diploma, UG, PG) whose parents' annual income does not exceed ₹2.5 lakh.
benefits: Full non-refundable compulsory tuition fee reimbursement (paid directly to institution or student) plus a monthly academic maintenance allowance of up to ₹13,500 per year (for hostellers in professional courses) and ₹7,000 per year (for day scholars). Also includes study tour allowances, thesis typing charges, and disability allowances.
estimatedBenefit: Full eligible fees + annual academic allowance
deadlineInfo: Announced annually for every academic session (usually opens in July/August and closes in November/December).

process: Step 1: Go to the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in.
Step 2: Generate your One-Time Registration (OTR) using your Aadhaar number and FaceRD / OTP authentication.
Step 3: Log in using your OTR number and password.
Step 4: Select 'Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment' -> 'Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students'.
Step 5: Fill in your academic details (Current Institute AISHE code, Course, Year of Study).
Step 6: Fill in Category, Family Annual Income, and Bank Account details.
Step 7: Upload required documents (Caste Certificate, Income Certificate, Marksheet, Fee Receipt, and Photo).
Step 8: Review the completed form and click 'Final Submit'.
Step 9: Download and print the application form and submit a physical copy with document copies to your College Nodal Officer (CNO).
Step 10: College verifies on portal (Level 1), District Welfare Officer approves (Level 2), and scholarship funds are released via DBT.

faqs.q: Can I apply if I am studying in a private unaided college?
faqs.a: Yes. Post Matric SC scholarship covers students enrolled in recognized private colleges, provided the course is approved by UGC, AICTE, MCI, or state regulatory bodies.

faqs.q: Is there any minimum percentage required in Class 10 or 12?
faqs.a: No minimum cut-off percentage is prescribed; students only need to pass the qualifying exam and obtain regular admission.

faqs.q: What should I do if my application is marked 'Defective'?
faqs.a: Log in to your NSP account immediately. The defect remark by your college will be displayed (e.g. 're-upload income certificate'). Upload the corrected file and re-submit.

faqs.q: Can I receive this scholarship and another merit scholarship simultaneously?
faqs.a: No. Under central guidelines, a student cannot hold two government scholarships simultaneously; you must choose the one offering higher benefits.

faqs.q: How much maintenance allowance does a hosteller get?
faqs.a: Hostellers in professional degree courses (Group 1: MBBS, B.Tech, M.Tech) receive up to ₹13,500 per year in maintenance allowance.

faqs.q: What is OTR on the National Scholarship Portal?
faqs.a: One Time Registration (OTR) is a unique 14-digit number assigned to a student upon Aadhaar facial/biometric verification on NSP, eliminating the need to re-register each year.

purpose: The Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, is the government's premier educational equity program. It provides comprehensive financial support to Scheduled Caste students studying at post-secondary and higher education levels, ensuring that poverty does not force talented students to drop out.
targetBeneficiary: Scheduled Caste (SC) students who have completed Class 10 and are pursuing recognized post-matriculation, undergraduate, postgraduate, doctoral, or professional/technical degree courses.
financialBenefit: 100% compulsory course fees reimbursed + maintenance allowance up to ₹13,500/year (Hosteller) or ₹7,000/year (Day Scholar)
benefitFrequency: Annual scholarship disbursed in two components (fee reimbursement and maintenance allowance)
impact: Dramatically increases higher education gross enrolment ratio (GER) among Scheduled Caste youth, enabling entry into professional careers in engineering, medicine, law, and research.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: No age ceiling, provided student is enrolled in a recognized post-matric course.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Total parental/family annual income from all sources must NOT exceed ₹2,50,000 per annum.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Passed Class 10 (Matriculation) from a recognized state/central board.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Student in regular full-time study (students in full-time employment are not eligible).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Strictly Scheduled Caste (SC) category as notified in the Presidential Order.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India permanent resident of the respective State/UT.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Up to two boys of the same parents can receive the scholarship; no limit applies to girls.

mandatoryConditions: Must belong to a Scheduled Caste (SC) community with valid caste certificate
Total family annual income must not exceed ₹2,50,000 per year
Must be admitted to a government-recognized school, college, polytechnic, or university
Student's bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded on the NPCI mapper for Direct Benefit Transfer
conditionalRequirements: Hostel resident certificate from warden required to claim the higher hosteller maintenance rate.
ineligibility: Students whose total family income exceeds ₹2,50,000 per annum
Students repeating the same stage of education in a different stream (e.g. passing B.A. and re-enrolling in B.Com)
Students pursuing education through distance mode who are concurrently in paid full-time employment
Beneficiaries receiving another parallel government scholarship or fellowship
applicationMode: Online via National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) or State Scholarship Portal
offlineProcess: While submission is 100% online on NSP, students must physically submit the printed acknowledgment copy, along with self-attested photocopies of all certificates, to their College Scholarship Section / Nodal Officer for electronic institutional verification on the portal.
commonMistakes: Student bank account not linked to Aadhaar for DBT: Merely linking Aadhaar for KYC does not activate the NPCI DBT mapper; students must specifically submit the 'Aadhaar DBT Mandate' at their bank.
Applying under wrong state domicile: The application must be filed in the student's home state of permanent residence, even if studying in another state.
Missing college institutional verification deadline: Colleges must approve online before the state deadline expires.
openingDate: Typically opens every year in July/August
processingTime: 60 to 90 days following institutional and state district verification cut-offs.
renewalRequired: Yes, students must apply for 'Renewal' every subsequent academic year after passing exams.
trackingProcedure: Log in to scholarships.gov.in using OTR / Application ID to view Level 1 (College), Level 2 (District), and PFMS payment status.
correctionProcedure: If application is marked 'Defective' by the college or district officer, it is returned to the student's portal for online correction within 7 days.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Student's Bank Account via PFMS and NPCI Aadhaar Bridge
disbursementDetails: Maintenance allowance and fee reimbursement amounts are released jointly by the Central Government (60%) and State Government (40%) directly into the student's bank account via PFMS.

name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
department: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
applyChannel: the National Scholarship Portal
description: Merit-cum-means scholarship for students who scored above the 80th percentile in their Class 12 board and are pursuing regular higher education.
whoCanApply: Students above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their Class 12 board, pursuing a regular degree course, with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh per year.
benefits: Direct financial cash scholarship: ₹12,000 per year at Graduation level for the first 3 years of college, and ₹20,000 per year at Postgraduate level (or 4th & 5th year of integrated professional courses like B.Tech / MBBS). Disbursed directly into the student's bank account annually.
deadlineInfo: Opens annually on NSP in July/August and closes in November/December.

Family income up to ₹4.5 lakh per year
Scored above the 80th percentile in Class 12 board results

documents.issuingAuthority: State Board of Secondary Education / CBSE / CISCE
documents.format: Original Marksheet copy certified by College Principal

documents.why: Proves enrollment in regular full-time undergraduate college course.

process: Step 1: Check your Class 12 State Board cut-off list to ensure your score is above the 80th percentile.
Step 2: Visit scholarships.gov.in and complete One-Time Registration (OTR) with Aadhaar.
Step 3: Log in and choose 'Department of Higher Education' -> 'Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students'.
Step 4: Enter your Class 12 Roll Number, Board Name, Year of Passing, and College AISHE code.
Step 5: Fill in your parent's annual income and bank account details.
Step 6: Upload the required documents (Marksheet, Income Certificate, Fee Receipt, and Photo).
Step 7: Submit the application and print the confirmation copy.
Step 8: Submit the printout and original verification documents to your College Nodal Officer.
Step 9: College Nodal Officer verifies your enrollment on the NSP institute portal.
Step 10: State Education Department approves, and funds are credited directly to your bank account via PFMS.

faqs.q: What is the 80th percentile cut-off?
faqs.a: Each state education board and CBSE publishes a specific cut-off mark for Science, Commerce, and Arts streams representing the top 20% of passing students. If your marks equal or exceed that cut-off, you are eligible.

faqs.q: How many scholarships are awarded nationally every year?
faqs.a: A total of 82,000 fresh scholarships are awarded every year across India (41,000 for boys and 41,000 for girls), allocated to states based on population.

faqs.q: Can I renew the scholarship if I have an academic backlog?
faqs.a: To renew, you must secure at least 50% marks in the annual college examination and maintain 75% attendance. Students failing their annual exam are not eligible for renewal.

faqs.q: Can engineering (B.Tech) and medical (MBBS) students receive this?
faqs.a: Yes. For 4-year engineering and 5-year medical degrees, students receive ₹12,000/year for the first 3 years and ₹20,000/year for the 4th and 5th years.

faqs.q: Is this scholarship available for postgraduate studies?
faqs.a: Yes, students who received the scholarship during graduation and transition to postgraduate studies (M.A., M.Sc., M.Com) continue receiving ₹20,000/year.

faqs.q: Do I need to submit an income certificate every year for renewal?
faqs.a: Yes, family income must be certified as remaining below ₹4.5 Lakh during renewal.

purpose: The Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (PM-USP), implemented by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, supports meritorious students from economically weaker sections to meet day-to-day expenses while pursuing university graduate and postgraduate degrees.
targetBeneficiary: Meritorious students who score above the 80th percentile of their respective state/central education board in Class 12 and are enrolled in regular full-time undergraduate courses.
financialBenefit: ₹12,000 per year for Graduation (Years 1–3) and ₹20,000 per year for Post-Graduation (Years 4–5)
benefitFrequency: Annual lump-sum disbursement for up to 5 years
impact: Rewards academic merit, relieves financial anxiety for college students, and enables students to purchase textbooks, laptops, and study materials without parental loans.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 18 to 25 years.
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: 50% of scholarships are reserved for girl students.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Gross family annual income must NOT exceed ₹4,50,000 per annum.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Class 12 pass with marks above the 80th percentile cut-off declared by the respective State Education Board / CBSE / CISCE.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Enrolled in a regular full-time degree program in a recognized university/college.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (General, OBC, SC, ST, EWS) distributed per state quotas.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Family income verified by Revenue authority.

mandatoryConditions: Must have scored above the 80th percentile in Class 12 board examination in the current academic year
Must be pursuing a regular, full-time undergraduate degree course recognized by UGC, AICTE, or government authorities
Total family annual income must be below ₹4,50,000 per year
Must maintain at least 50% marks in university exams and 75% attendance for annual renewal
conditionalRequirements: Board percentile verification slip issued by the respective state board / CBSE.
ineligibility: Students pursuing diploma courses, distance education, or correspondence courses
Students who have scored below the board's 80th percentile merit cut-off
Students receiving any other state or central government scholarship or fee waiver
Family annual income exceeding ₹4,50,000
applicationMode: Online via National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in)
offlineProcess: Submit the physical copy of your NSP application form and attested photocopies of your 12th marksheet, income certificate, and fee receipt to your college scholarship counter.
commonMistakes: Applying with diploma enrollment: The scheme is strictly for degree courses (B.A., B.Sc., B.Com, B.Tech, MBBS, etc.); diploma polytechnics are ineligible.
Failing to renew after 1st year: Students must apply for renewal every year on NSP with a marksheet showing at least 50% marks in college exams.
Name discrepancy between 12th marksheet and Aadhaar: Causes rejection at board matching stage.

renewalRequired: Yes, annual renewal required on NSP with at least 50% marks and 75% attendance.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on scholarships.gov.in using OTR / Application ID.
correctionProcedure: Request college nodal officer to reject application to 'Defective' status to enable online editing.

faqs.q: What is Kutumba ID in Karnataka SSP?
faqs.a: Kutumba is the Karnataka Government's unified family database. It automatically identifies all family members, their caste, and land ownership, eliminating repetitive document submissions.

faqs.q: What is e-Attestation and how do I get it?
faqs.a: e-Attestation is the process where a designated officer in your college verifies your original fee receipt and marksheet and approves it digitally on the eattest.karnataka.gov.in portal.

faqs.q: What is the income limit for Category 2A, 2B, 3A, and 3B students?
faqs.a: The annual family income must be less than ₹1,00,000 per annum for Category 2A, 2B, 3A, and 3B.

faqs.q: Can students in private engineering colleges get fee reimbursement?
faqs.a: Yes, CET/KEA quota students in private engineering and medical colleges receive full or partial fee reimbursement as approved by the government.

faqs.q: What is Vidyasiri scholarship on SSP?
faqs.a: Vidyasiri provides monthly food and accommodation allowances (up to ₹1,500/month) for students who do not get admission into government departmental hostels.

faqs.q: How can I verify if my bank account is seeded with Aadhaar?
faqs.a: Visit the Karnataka DBT portal (dbt.karnataka.gov.in) and click 'Know Your Aadhaar Seeding Status'.

purpose: State Scholarship Portal (SSP) Post-Matric Scholarship is an integrated digital welfare initiative of the Government of Karnataka combining scholarships across Social Welfare, Tribal Welfare, Backward Classes Welfare, and Minorities Welfare departments to automate seamless fee reimbursement and hostel food allowances for Karnataka students.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: SC/ST: up to ₹2,50,000 per year; Category-1: up to ₹2,50,000; 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B: up to ₹1,00,000 per year.

detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: SC, ST, Category-1, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, and Religious Minorities.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Covered per student record.

benefits: Direct financial support of ₹6,000 per year transferred directly into the bank accounts of eligible farmer families in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 every four months (April–July, August–November, and December–March).
deadlineInfo: Continuous year-round scheme. Applications submitted and verified before an installment cut-off receive that upcoming installment.

Step 3: Enter your Aadhaar number, Mobile Number, select your State, and submit the Captcha.

Step 5: Fill in your complete State, District, Sub-District, Block, and Village.

faqs.q: Can both husband and wife receive PM-KISAN benefits?
faqs.a: No. The scheme defines a family as husband, wife, and minor children. Only one person per family can receive PM-KISAN, even if both own separate plots of land.

faqs.q: Why was my PM-KISAN instalment stopped?
faqs.a: The three most common reasons are: 1) Pending e-KYC, 2) Land seeding not marked 'Yes' by the state revenue department, or 3) Bank account not mapped to NPCI for Aadhaar-based DBT.

faqs.q: Can tenant farmers cultivating leased land apply?
faqs.a: No. PM-KISAN requires ownership of cultivable land in official state land records. Tenant farmers without land titles are not eligible.

faqs.q: What should I do if my bank account changed?
faqs.a: Since PM-KISAN uses Aadhaar-based payments, payments automatically route to whichever bank account is actively seeded with Aadhaar on NPCI. You do not need to update bank details on the portal—simply visit your preferred bank and submit the Aadhaar DBT Seeding Mandate.

faqs.q: Can a government servant who owns farmland apply?
faqs.a: No. All regular government employees (central, state, PSUs, autonomous bodies) are strictly excluded from PM-KISAN, except Class IV / Multi-Tasking staff.

faqs.q: How can I find my PM-KISAN Registration Number?
faqs.a: Visit pmkisan.gov.in, click 'Know Your Status', click 'Know Your Registration Number', and enter your Aadhaar number or mobile number to retrieve your registration ID.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a central sector flagship scheme introduced to provide income support to all landholding farmer families across India, helping them procure agricultural inputs like seeds, fertilizers, and farm equipment while preventing reliance on informal moneylenders.
targetBeneficiary: All landholding farmer families who have cultivable land registered in their name in state land records.
financialBenefit: ₹6,000 per year (3 equal instalments of ₹2,000 every 4 months via Direct Benefit Transfer / DBT)
benefitFrequency: Every 4 months (Thrice annually)
impact: Provides assured liquidity to small and marginal farmers before sowing and harvesting seasons, reduces agricultural distress, and supports rural household consumption.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 18 years and above (farmer head of household).
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Both male and female landholding farmers.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No specific gross income ceiling, but farmer must not fall into any of the specified institutional or income-tax exclusion categories.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to farmers of all categories (General, OBC, SC, ST).
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India residing in rural or peri-urban agricultural zones.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: A farmer family is defined as husband, wife, and minor children. Only one person per family can receive PM-KISAN benefits for the family's landholding.

mandatoryConditions: Cultivable land record (Khatoni / RoR / 7/12 / Patta) must be registered in the name of the farmer in the state revenue portal
Mandatory e-KYC completed on pmkisan.gov.in via Aadhaar OTP or biometric scan
Bank account must be active, Aadhaar-seeded, and mapped to the NPCI DBT mapper
State government revenue authority must verify land ownership and approve the beneficiary record
conditionalRequirements: Mutation / registry certificate required if land was inherited after the baseline cut-off date (1 February 2019)
ineligibility: All institutional landholders (land owned by trusts, companies, religious institutions)
Farmer families holding or having held constitutional posts (Ministers, MPs, MLAs, Mayors, Zila Panchayat Chairpersons)
Serving or retired officers and employees of central/state government ministries, departments, autonomous bodies, and PSUs (excluding multi-tasking / Class IV / Group D staff)
All superannuated / retired pensioners whose monthly pension is ₹10,000 or more
All persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year
Professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects registered with professional bodies
applicationMode: Online via PM-KISAN Portal / App or Offline via CSC / Local Patwari / Agriculture Office
offlineProcess: Visit your local Village Patwari / Lekhpal, Block Agriculture Officer (BAO), or nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Carry your original Aadhaar Card, updated Land Khatauni / Jamabandi, and Bank Passbook. The CSC operator will submit your application on the Kisan portal, record your biometric thumbprint, and provide an acknowledgement receipt.
commonMistakes: Bank Account not seeded with Aadhaar on NPCI: Payment fails if the bank account is merely linked for KYC but not mapped for DBT on NPCI server.
Land Record in Ancestor's Name: If land is still in deceased parent's name, the heir must complete land mutation (Dakhil-Kharij) first.
Spelling of name on portal differing from Aadhaar database: Causes automated Aadhaar rejection during installment processing.
Income tax filing: If any family member files ITR (even refund), the system auto-detects and cancels registration with recovery notices.
processingTime: Typically 30 to 60 days for state revenue and agriculture department verification.
renewalRequired: No annual renewal required, but periodic e-KYC authentication must be completed every year.
trackingProcedure: Click 'Know Your Status' on pmkisan.gov.in, enter your Registration Number or Mobile number, and view your installment payment history and DBT status.
correctionProcedure: Use 'Name Correction as per Aadhaar' or visit your District Agriculture Office / PM-KISAN Grievance desk on the portal to resolve payment stop orders.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Bank Account via Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and NPCI
disbursementDetails: Funds of ₹2,000 are deposited directly into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked savings bank account every 4 months. Beneficiaries receive a direct SMS from the central PFMS/bank upon credit.

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
applyChannel: the PMFBY portal, your bank, CSC or insurance company
description: Crop insurance protecting farmers against yield losses from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
whoCanApply: Farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas.
benefits: Comprehensive insurance coverage from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages. Farmers pay a minimal premium of only 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops; the remaining actuarial premium (often 85–90%) is fully subsidized by Central and State Governments. Full claim compensation is credited directly via DBT.
estimatedBenefit: Crop loss compensation at low premium
deadlineInfo: Strict seasonal deadlines. Kharif deadline is typically 31 July; Rabi deadline is typically 31 December (subject to state notification).

Step 2: Click on 'Farmer Corner' and choose 'Apply for Crop Insurance by yourself'.
Step 3: Register or log in with your mobile number and verify via OTP.
Step 4: Enter farmer profile details, Aadhaar number, and residential address.
Step 5: Enter Bank account details where claim payments will be transferred.
Step 6: Select the Crop Details: Season (Kharif/Rabi), Year, State, District, Sub-district, Gram Panchayat, and Notified Crop.
Step 7: Enter Land details (Khata / Survey Number and insured area in hectares).

Step 9: Calculate premium (e.g. 2% for rice/paddy) and pay securely online through UPI/Net Banking.
Step 10: Download the Crop Insurance Policy Receipt with your Insurance Application Number.

faqs.q: Is crop insurance mandatory for loan-taking farmers?
faqs.a: No. PMFBY was made 100% voluntary for all farmers since Kharif 2020. However, loanee farmers must submit a written opt-out declaration to their bank at least 7 days before cut-off if they do not wish to be insured.

faqs.q: What is the maximum premium a farmer pays?
faqs.a: Farmers pay only 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for horticultural/commercial crops like cotton, chilies, or sugarcane.

faqs.q: How do I report crop damage from a hailstorm?
faqs.a: Open the Crop Insurance App on your phone, click 'Crop Loss Intimation', enter your policy number, upload photos of the damaged field with GPS coordinates, and submit within 72 hours.

faqs.q: Can sharecroppers or tenant farmers apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Tenant farmers and sharecroppers can insure crops by providing a tenancy agreement or sowing declaration from the village revenue authority.

faqs.q: What if drought prevents me from sowing my crop?
faqs.a: PMFBY includes a 'Prevented Sowing' provision. If major adverse weather prevents over 75% of sowing in a notified area, insured farmers receive up to 25% of sum insured as immediate relief.

faqs.q: Can I check my claim amount online?
faqs.a: Yes. Log in to pmfby.gov.in using your mobile number or policy number to view the sanctioned claim amount and bank transaction reference.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare to provide comprehensive financial insurance against crop loss caused by non-preventable natural risks (drought, flood, unseasonal rains, pest attacks, hailstorms), safeguarding farmers' investments and stabilizing farm income.
targetBeneficiary: All farmers (including sharecroppers and tenant farmers) growing notified crops in notified insurance areas.
financialBenefit: Comprehensive claim payout up to full Sum Insured (cost of cultivation/yield value) based on crop cutting experiments & localized damage assessments
benefitFrequency: Per Crop Season (Kharif and Rabi)
impact: Protects farmers against catastrophic bankruptcy due to monsoon failure, hailstorms, floods, or cyclones; enables continued investment in modern agriculture.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 18 years and above.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Farmer growing notified crops on owned, leased, or sharecropped land.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories (General, SC, ST, OBC).
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of India with agricultural holding in notified crop areas.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Covered per farmer / plot entry.

mandatoryConditions: Must be growing a notified crop in a notified block/gram panchayat for that specific season
Must insure crop and pay farmer premium before the cut-off date (usually 31 July for Kharif and 31 December for Rabi)
Must possess valid land record or registered tenancy agreement / sowing certificate
conditionalRequirements: Localized losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation) must be reported within 72 hours of occurrence on the Crop Insurance App or helpline.
ineligibility: Crops not notified by the respective State Government for insurance in that particular district/block
Losses arising from war, nuclear hazards, malicious damage, preventable negligence, or stray cattle grazing
Applications submitted after the seasonal cut-off date
Post-harvest losses occurring after 14 days of crop cutting or harvest
applicationMode: Online via pmfby.gov.in / Crop Insurance App & Offline via Bank Branches, CSCs, or PACs
offlineProcess: Farmers with KCC (Kisan Credit Card) loans can have insurance deducted automatically through their lending bank branch unless they opt out in writing. Non-loanee farmers can visit their nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) with land papers, sowing certificate, Aadhaar, and premium payment.
commonMistakes: Missing the 72-hour reporting deadline for localized damage: For hailstorms or unseasonal flood inundation, claims must be registered within 72 hours via the Crop Insurance App or toll-free 14447.
Entering wrong survey or khata number: Leads to claim disqualification during satellite/remote sensing cross-checks.
Mismatch between insured crop and actual sown crop: If a farmer insured paddy but later sowed pulses without notifying the bank, the claim is rejected.
openingDate: Kharif enrolment opens in April/May; Rabi enrolment opens in October/November
processingTime: Mid-season adversity claims paid within 30 days of survey; final seasonal yield claims paid within 3 weeks of Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) data upload.
renewalRequired: Yes, required fresh for every crop season (Kharif and Rabi).
trackingProcedure: Enter your 10-digit Application Number on pmfby.gov.in under 'Application Status' to track policy issuance and claim calculation.
correctionProcedure: Visit your lending bank branch or CSC before the cut-off date to request crop change or area adjustments.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Farmer's Bank Account via National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP)
disbursementDetails: Insurance companies calculate claims based on automated yield loss data from Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and satellite index data. Claim amounts are credited directly into farmers' bank accounts via PFMS.

Step 2: Choose 'Citizen Assessment' and enter your Aadhaar Number to verify identity.
Step 3: Select your application category: 'Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC)' if you have land, or 'Credit Linked Subsidy (CLSS)' if taking a home loan.

faqs.q: What is PMAY-U 2.0?
faqs.a: Launched in August 2024, PMAY-Urban 2.0 is the expanded flagship urban housing program with a budget of ₹10 lakh crore to provide 1 crore urban poor and middle-class families with pucca houses over the next 5 years.

faqs.q: Is female ownership mandatory under PMAY?
faqs.a: Yes! A core pillar of PMAY is women's empowerment: the pucca house must be registered in the name of an adult female member or jointly in the name of husband and wife.

faqs.q: How much subsidy does an urban homeowner receive for building a house on their own plot?
faqs.a: Under the Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC) component, eligible EWS families receive ₹1,50,000 from the Central Government, plus ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000 from the State Government, totaling up to ₹2.5 Lakh in direct construction grants.

faqs.q: How does the home loan interest subsidy work under PMAY?
faqs.a: Under the Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS), the government provides up to a 4.0% interest subsidy on home loans up to ₹25 Lakh for houses valued up to ₹35 Lakh, crediting up to ₹1.80 Lakh upfront into your loan account.

faqs.q: Can a family owning an ancestral village house apply for PMAY-Urban?
faqs.a: The family must not own any pucca house anywhere in India. If the village home is a kutcha mud house, you remain eligible.

faqs.q: What is the geo-tagging inspection?
faqs.a: Municipal engineers visit your plot and capture GPS-stamped photographs at 4 stages: 1) Vacant plot, 2) Foundation level, 3) Lintel/Roof level, and 4) Fully completed house with painted PMAY logo.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U 2.0), under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, aims to provide all-weather pucca houses with basic civic infrastructure (water, sanitation, electricity, and kitchen) to all eligible urban families belonging to EWS, LIG, and Middle Income Groups across India.
targetBeneficiary: Urban poor and middle-class families belonging to Economically Weaker Section (EWS - income < ₹3L), Low Income Group (LIG - income ₹3L–₹6L), and Middle Income Group (MIG - income ₹6L–₹9L) who do not own a pucca house anywhere in India.
financialBenefit: Direct grant of ₹1.5 to ₹2.5 Lakh (BLC) OR upfront home loan interest subsidy up to ₹1.80 Lakh (CLSS/ISS)
benefitFrequency: Milestone-based construction grant or upfront loan interest subsidy
impact: Fulfills the dream of home ownership for urban slum dwellers, informal workers, and middle-class families, providing secure legal title registered in the name of the female head of the family.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Adult head of family (18+ years).
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Mandatory female ownership or co-ownership (house must be registered in the name of female head or jointly with husband).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (EWS, LIG, SC, ST, OBC, General).
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of statutory town / urban local body.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Beneficiary family (husband, wife, unmarried children) must not own a pucca house anywhere in India.

mandatoryConditions: The beneficiary family must NOT own a pucca house in their name anywhere in India
The house must be registered in the name of an adult female member or jointly with her husband (sole male ownership permitted only in absence of adult female in family)
Carpet area must be up to 30 sq.m for EWS and up to 60 sq.m for LIG
For BLC component, applicant must own a vacant plot of land in an urban municipal area
conditionalRequirements: Building plan approval from urban local body required before construction grant release.
ineligibility: Families that already own a pucca house anywhere in India
Families that have previously received financial assistance under any central/state housing scheme (e.g. earlier PMAY, RAY, VAMBAY)
Annual household income exceeding ₹9,00,000
applicationMode: Online via PMAY-U Portal (pmaymis.gov.in) / PMAY-U 2.0 App or through Municipal Corporation / CSC
offlineProcess: Visit the Housing Section at your local Municipal Corporation or Town Municipality office. Officials assist with online registration and schedule the geo-tagging site inspection.
commonMistakes: Registering only in male member's name: The law strictly mandates that the house title must be in the name of the female head or joint ownership.
Building without municipal plan sanction: BLC grants require formal municipal building plan approval before first foundation tranche is disbursed.
Commencing construction before geo-tagging: Municipal engineers must geo-tag the vacant plot BEFORE construction begins; unverified structures are rejected.
processingTime: Sanctioned within 60 to 90 days; construction funds disbursed over 12 to 18 months per milestone.
renewalRequired: One-time housing grant per family.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on pmaymis.gov.in under 'Search Beneficiary' using Aadhaar or Assessment ID.
correctionProcedure: Municipal housing officer can update applicant data on the PMAY-MIS portal before state sanction.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Beneficiary Bank Account (BLC) OR Upfront Interest Credit to Bank (CLSS)
disbursementDetails: For Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC), grants (₹1.5L–₹2.5L) are credited in 3–4 tranches into the female head's bank account linked to geo-tagged photo verification. For home loans (CLSS), the central subsidy is paid upfront to the lending bank, immediately reducing the borrower's loan principal and monthly EMI.

name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin
department: Ministry of Rural Development
applyChannel: your Gram Panchayat / Block office
description: Financial assistance for houseless rural households and those living in kutcha or dilapidated houses to build a pucca house.
whoCanApply: Rural households that are houseless or live in kutcha houses, identified through SECC 2011 / Awaas+ surveys and verified by the Gram Sabha.
benefits: Direct financial grant of ₹1,20,000 in plain rural areas and ₹1,30,000 in hilly/difficult/northeastern/tribal states (disbursed in 3–4 milestone installments directly via DBT). In addition, beneficiaries receive 90 to 95 days of unskilled manual labor wages (approx ₹25,000) under MGNREGA for constructing their own house, plus ₹12,000 for toilet construction under Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), and a free Ujjwala LPG gas connection.
deadlineInfo: Union Cabinet approved the continuation of PMAY-G in August 2024 to construct 2 crore additional rural homes through March 2029.

process: Step 1: Check your family's name on the permanent PMAY-G priority list at your Gram Panchayat or on pmayg.nic.in.
Step 2: Gram Sabha verifies and approves the annual village priority ranking list.
Step 3: Block Development Officer (BDO) issues the formal Sanction Order for your house.
Step 4: Village Gram Rozgar Sevak (GRS) visits your site and uploads Geo-tagged photos of your existing kutcha house on the 'AwaasApp'.
Step 5: First installment (approx ₹25,000–₹40,000) is credited directly to your bank account via PFMS.
Step 6: Complete the foundation work; GRS captures geo-tagged photos of the plinth level.
Step 7: Second installment (approx ₹40,000–₹45,000) is credited to raise walls to lintel level.
Step 8: Construct walls and roof; GRS captures third geo-tagged inspection photos.
Step 9: Final installment is released upon roof casting, door/window fitting, and toilet construction.
Step 10: House is painted with the mandatory PMAY-G logo, and your electricity and Ujjwala gas connection are installed.

faqs.q: What is the total financial benefit a rural family receives under PMAY-G?
faqs.a: A rural family receives: 1) ₹1,20,000 construction grant (or ₹1,30,000 in hill states), 2) approx ₹25,000 as 90–95 days of MGNREGA wages, 3) ₹12,000 for toilet construction under Swachh Bharat Mission, and 4) free Ujjwala LPG connection, totaling around ₹1,60,000+ in benefits.

faqs.q: Can I choose my own design and building materials for my house?
faqs.a: Yes! Beneficiaries can build using locally available materials (burnt brick, stone, mud-mortar, bamboo) suited to local disaster risks (earthquake, flood, cyclone), as long as the roof is permanent and area is at least 25 sq.m.

faqs.q: Who decides who gets a house first in the village?
faqs.a: The priority list is generated automatically based on SECC 2011 deprivation points (houseless, zero-room, single-room kutcha, female-headed, SC/ST) and must be formally verified and approved by the open Gram Sabha.

faqs.q: Can a family take an additional bank loan to make a bigger house?
faqs.a: Yes. PMAY-G beneficiaries can avail an optional institutional bank loan of up to ₹70,000 at concessional interest rates to expand their house.

faqs.q: What should I do if a local official asks for a bribe to release my installment?
faqs.a: Never pay a bribe. Installments are disbursed 100% electronically via DBT from central treasury directly to your bank account. Report extortion directly to the District Collector or call the central rural grievance helpline at 1800-11-6446.

faqs.q: What is the AwaasApp mobile application?
faqs.a: AwaasApp is the official mobile application used by village inspectors to capture geo-tagged, time-stamped photographs of your house construction at every stage to trigger the next installment payment.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), under the Ministry of Rural Development, provides direct financial assistance to homeless rural families and those living in kutcha, dilapidated houses to construct a quality pucca house with basic amenities including electricity, piped water, and an LPG connection, fulfilling the national goal of 'Housing for All'.
targetBeneficiary: Rural households identified as houseless or living in zero, one, or two-room kutcha houses as per the SECC 2011 deprivation index and the Awas+ rural housing survey.
financialBenefit: Direct construction grant of ₹1,20,000 (plains) / ₹1,30,000 (hills) + ₹25,000 MGNREGA wages + ₹12,000 toilet grant
benefitFrequency: Milestone-based construction grant disbursed in 3–4 tranches via DBT
impact: Has constructed over 2.6 crore rural homes across India with disaster-resilient local architecture, transforming rural living standards and creating permanent family assets in women's names.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Adult head of household (18+ years).
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: House is registered in the name of the woman or jointly in the name of husband and wife.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Assessed based on rural deprivation criteria in SECC 2011 and Awas+ surveys.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Rural agricultural laborer, artisan, informal worker, marginal farmer.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories; high priority quotas for SC, ST, primitive tribes, and minorities.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Family (husband, wife, and minor children) must not own a pucca house anywhere in India.

Must not own a pucca house anywhere in India
Minimum carpet area of constructed house must be at least 25 sq. metres with a dedicated hygienic cooking space
Bank account must be seeded with Aadhaar for Direct Benefit Transfer via AwaasSoft

Households with any family member who is a regular government employee
Households paying income tax or professional tax

Households owning an existing pucca house with concrete roof

commonMistakes: Employing private contractors: PMAY-G strictly encourages beneficiaries to construct their own homes or hire local masons; private contractors are banned by guidelines.
Building smaller than 25 sq. metres: Houses with carpet area under 25 sq. metres are disqualified for final installment payment.
Not completing toilet: Final payment requires completion of a functional sanitary toilet.
processingTime: House construction typically completed over 6 to 12 months in 3–4 phased installments.
renewalRequired: One-time lifetime housing grant.
trackingProcedure: Visit pmayg.nic.in, click 'Stakeholders' -> 'IAY/PMAYG Beneficiary' and enter your 7-digit PMAY-G Registration ID to view installment status and inspection photos.
correctionProcedure: Gram Panchayat Secretary or BDO can update bank accounts on AwaasSoft upon biometric verification.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Beneficiary's Bank Account via AwaasSoft & PFMS
disbursementDetails: Grants (₹1,20,000 in plains / ₹1,30,000 in hills) are transferred in 3–4 milestone installments directly into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked savings account upon automated approval of geo-tagged inspection photos.

name: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)
department: Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
applyChannel: the PMUY portal or your nearest LPG distributor
description: Deposit-free LPG connections to adult women from poor households to promote clean cooking fuel.
whoCanApply: Adult women from poor households with no existing LPG connection in the household, belonging to listed categories (e.g., SC/ST, PMAY-G, AAY, forest dwellers) or declaring poverty under the 14-point declaration.
benefits: Free LPG connection with zero deposit fee: Government covers the security deposit of the 14.2 kg cylinder, pressure regulator, LPG hose pipe, domestic gas consumer card (DGCC booklet), and installation charges. Beneficiaries receive their first 14.2 kg LPG refill completely free along with a free two-burner gas stove (hotplate). In addition, beneficiaries receive an ongoing targeted central subsidy of ₹300 per refill (up to 12 refills per year) credited via DBT.
deadlineInfo: Universal ongoing scheme under Ujjwala 2.0. Applications are accepted year-round.

Holds a ration card (indicator of poor household)
Belongs to an eligible poor-household category or submits the 14-point declaration

process: Step 1: Visit pmuy.gov.in or go directly to your nearest local Indane, Bharatgas, or HP Gas distributor.
Step 2: Select 'Apply for New Ujjwala 2.0 Connection' and choose your preferred LPG distributor.
Step 3: Fill in applicant's personal details, family members' names, and address.
Step 4: Provide Aadhaar numbers of the applicant and all adult family members.
Step 5: Provide bank details (Account number and IFSC) for subsidy transfer.
Step 6: Submit application online or hand over the filled form at the gas agency.
Step 7: Distributor conducts electronic de-duplication to verify no existing connection exists in your home.
Step 8: Application is approved and subscription voucher (SV) is generated.
Step 9: Visit the gas agency to collect your free LPG cylinder, regulator, safety hose pipe, two-burner stove, and passbook.
Step 10: The gas agency technician delivers the setup to your kitchen and provides safety training.

faqs.q: Is the first refill and gas stove really free?
faqs.a: Yes! Under Ujjwala 2.0, the government provides the first 14.2 kg gas cylinder refill and a brand-new ISI-marked two-burner gas stove completely free of cost.

faqs.q: How much subsidy is credited per refill?
faqs.a: Eligible Ujjwala beneficiaries receive a targeted subsidy of ₹300 per 14.2 kg cylinder directly in their bank account for up to 12 refills every financial year.

faqs.q: Can migrant workers living in rented rooms apply without local domicile?
faqs.a: Yes! Ujjwala 2.0 has special provisions for migrant workers. You only need to submit a self-declaration for your family composition and current rented address.

faqs.q: Can men apply for PMUY?
faqs.a: No. The scheme is specifically designed for women's empowerment; the gas connection is legally registered exclusively in the name of an adult female family member.

faqs.q: Can I choose between a 14.2 kg and a 5 kg cylinder?
faqs.a: Yes. Beneficiaries can opt for either a standard 14.2 kg cylinder or a 5 kg double-cylinder connection for easier handling.

faqs.q: How do I book a refill after getting the connection?
faqs.a: You can book a refill by giving a missed call to your gas company's designated number, via WhatsApp booking, using the Bharat/IndianOil/HP Pay app, or through UMANG.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), implemented by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, provides clean cooking LPG connections to adult women from poor households, eliminating indoor air pollution caused by burning firewood and coal, safeguarding women's respiratory health, and empowering female heads of households.
targetBeneficiary: Adult women (18+ years) belonging to poor and deprived households who do not have an existing LPG connection in their household.
financialBenefit: Free LPG connection worth ₹1,600 + Free first 14.2 kg refill + Free two-burner gas stove + ₹300 subsidy per refill via DBT
benefitFrequency: One-time free connection kit + ongoing ₹300 per refill subsidy (up to 12 refills annually)
impact: Prevents chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and eye damage from kitchen smoke, saves millions of hours of firewood gathering for rural women, and enhances home safety.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Must be an adult woman aged 18 years or older.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Must belong to Below Poverty Line (BPL) or eligible poor household categories under SECC 2011 / 14-point declaration.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Priority for SC, ST, PM Awas Gramin, Antyodaya (AAY), Most Backward Classes, Tea garden tribes, and forest dwellers.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: No existing active LPG connection of any oil marketing company (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL) in the same household.

mandatoryConditions: Applicant must be an adult woman aged 18 years or older
No other active domestic LPG connection must exist in the household across all family members listed on the Ration Card
Must have an individual Aadhaar-seeded bank account for receiving ₹300 refill subsidy
conditionalRequirements: 14-point self-declaration required for non-SECC poor households under Ujjwala 2.0.
ineligibility: Households that already possess an active domestic LPG connection
Male applicants
Households where family members pay income tax or own four-wheelers
applicationMode: Online via pmuy.gov.in or Offline at any Indane, Bharatgas, or HP Gas distributorship
offlineProcess: Walk into your local Indane, Bharat Gas, or HP Gas showroom. Collect the free Ujjwala 2.0 application form. Attach photocopies of your Ration Card, your Aadhaar, family Aadhaar cards, and bank passbook. The distributor will register your biometric e-KYC on the spot.
commonMistakes: Another family member already has a gas cylinder: Central LPG database detects existing connections in the household and rejects duplicate requests.
Migrant workers without local address proof: Under Ujjwala 2.0, migrant families do NOT need local address proof; a simple self-declaration of address is accepted.
Bank account not mapped to NPCI: Prevents crediting the ₹300 refill subsidy.
processingTime: Connection issued within 7 to 10 working days from document verification.
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; cylinder refills can be booked by IVR/WhatsApp/mobile app anytime.
trackingProcedure: Call your local LPG distributor or check status on mylpg.in using your reference number.
correctionProcedure: Visit your gas distributor to update mobile numbers or bank accounts.
disbursementMethod: Direct Physical Equipment Delivery at Gas Distributorship + Refill Subsidy via DBT (PAHAL)
disbursementDetails: The cylinder, stove, and regulator are handed over physically at zero cost. When purchasing subsequent refills at market price, the ₹300 central subsidy is credited into the woman's bank account within 48 hours via PFMS/DBT.
helpline: Ujjwala Toll-Free Helpline: 1800-266-6696 or 1906 (24/7 LPG Emergency)

name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
department: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), Ministry of Finance
applyChannel: your bank branch, net banking, or the Jan Suraksha portal
description: Voluntary pension scheme that gives a guaranteed minimum monthly pension after age 60 based on your contributions.
whoCanApply: Indian citizens aged 18–40 with a savings bank account who are not (and have not been) income-tax payers.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 per month starting from age 60 until death. Upon subscriber's death, the exact same pension is paid to the spouse for life. Upon the death of both subscriber and spouse, the entire accumulated pension wealth (corpus up to ₹8.5 Lakh) is returned 100% to the designated nominee.
deadlineInfo: Can be joined anytime between ages 18 and 40. Open year-round.

process: Step 1: Visit the bank branch or post office where you maintain your savings bank account, or log in to your bank's Net Banking app.
Step 2: Search for 'Atal Pension Yojana (APY)' under Government Schemes / Social Security.
Step 3: Select your desired monthly pension slab (₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000/month).
Step 4: The system auto-calculates your monthly contribution based on your current age (e.g., at age 18, only ₹210/month for a ₹5,000 pension).
Step 5: Provide Spouse details and Nominee details.
Step 6: Authorize the monthly auto-debit mandate from your savings account.
Step 7: Submit the application. Your Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) is generated immediately.
Step 8: Download or collect your APY e-PRAN Card from the NSDL-CRA portal (npscra.nsdl.co.in).
Step 9: Monthly contributions are deducted automatically until you turn 60 years old.
Step 10: Upon turning 60, submit your pension claim form at your bank; your guaranteed monthly pension begins immediately.

faqs.q: Is the pension amount guaranteed by the Government of India?
faqs.a: Yes! Atal Pension Yojana carries an explicit statutory guarantee from the Government of India. Even if the accumulated fund underperforms, the central government funds any deficit to ensure you receive the full pension.

faqs.q: What happens to the money if the subscriber dies after age 60?
faqs.a: Upon subscriber's demise, the exact same monthly pension continues to the spouse for life. After the spouse passes away, the entire accumulated corpus (up to ₹8.5 Lakh for a ₹5,000 slab) is paid 100% to the nominee.

faqs.q: Can I increase or decrease my pension amount later?
faqs.a: Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade your pension slab (e.g. from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000) once every financial year through your bank.

faqs.q: Can income tax payers enroll in APY?
faqs.a: No. Since 1 October 2022, citizens who are or have been income tax payers are not eligible to join APY.

faqs.q: Can I exit the scheme before age 60?
faqs.a: Voluntary exit before 60 is permitted. The subscriber receives back their total accumulated contributions along with net interest earned, minus account maintenance charges.

faqs.q: How much do I need to contribute per month at age 18?
faqs.a: If you join at age 18, you pay only ₹42/month for a ₹1,000 pension, or ₹210/month for the maximum ₹5,000 monthly pension.

purpose: Atal Pension Yojana (APY), administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) under the Ministry of Finance, is India's flagship guaranteed social security pension scheme for unorganized sector workers, providing a lifelong monthly income from age 60.
targetBeneficiary: All Indian citizens aged 18 to 40 years working in the unorganized sector who do not pay income tax.
financialBenefit: Guaranteed lifelong pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month + 100% return of pension corpus to nominee
benefitFrequency: Monthly guaranteed pension from age 60 for lifetime
impact: Builds a formal pension safety net for informal workers, maidservants, delivery agents, small shopkeepers, and drivers, ensuring dignified old age security backed by sovereign government guarantee.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Must NOT be an income tax payer (effective 1 October 2022).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Informal, self-employed, daily wage, gig workers, and unorganized workers.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Individual subscriber account.

Must hold an active savings bank account or post office savings account
Must NOT be or have been an income tax payer under the Income Tax Act
Must set up auto-debit facility for monthly/quarterly contribution

Persons below 18 years or above 40 years of age

processingTime: PRAN generated within 24 to 48 hours.
renewalRequired: Auto-debit continues automatically every month until age 60.
trackingProcedure: Download APY mobile app or visit npscra.nsdl.co.in and enter your PRAN to view accumulated balance and statements.
correctionProcedure: Submit an APY Modification Form at your bank branch to change pension slab, address, or nominee.
disbursementMethod: Direct Monthly Pension Credit to Subscriber's Savings Bank Account
disbursementDetails: From age 60, PFRDA deposits the guaranteed monthly pension directly into the subscriber's savings bank account on the first week of every month for life.

department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance

description: Low-cost one-year renewable life insurance for bank account holders.

benefits: Guaranteed life insurance coverage of ₹2,00,000 payable to the nominee upon the death of the insured member due to any cause (natural death, illness, medical condition, or accident) for an ultra-affordable annual premium of just ₹436 per year (roughly ₹1.20 per day).
deadlineInfo: Can be joined anytime during the year (pro-rata premium applies for joining in later quarters); annual renewal in May.

process: Step 1: Log in to your bank's Net Banking app or visit your savings bank branch.
Step 2: Navigate to 'Insurance' -> 'Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)'.
Step 3: Confirm your Personal Details, Date of Birth, and Nominee details (Name, Relationship, Aadhaar).
Step 4: Authorize the annual auto-debit consent of ₹436 from your account.
Step 5: Submit the form. Certificate of Insurance (COI) is generated immediately.
Step 6: Premium of ₹436 is deducted automatically every year between 25 May and 31 May for renewal.
Step 7: In the unfortunate event of the insured's demise, the nominee submits the Claim Form and Death Certificate to the bank branch.
Step 8: Bank verifies records and forwards claim to the life insurance company (LIC/private insurer).

faqs.q: What does PMJJBY cover?
faqs.a: PMJJBY covers death due to ANY reason—natural death, heart attack, cancer, medical illness, or accidental death. The nominee receives ₹2,00,000.

faqs.q: What is the annual premium for PMJJBY?
faqs.a: The annual premium is only ₹436 per year (less than ₹1.20 per day), which is auto-debited once a year from your savings account.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for PMJJBY?
faqs.a: You can enroll between 18 and 50 years of age. Coverage continues up to 55 years of age, provided annual premiums are paid.

faqs.q: Is a medical checkup required to join?
faqs.a: No! No medical tests or health checkups are required. You only need to sign a simple self-certification of good health.

faqs.q: What is the 30-day lien period?
faqs.a: For fresh enrollments, claims for deaths occurring due to illness during the first 30 days are not covered (to prevent fraud). However, accidental deaths are covered from day one.

faqs.q: How much does PMSBY cost per year?
faqs.a: PMSBY costs an unbelievable ₹20 per year (raised from ₹12 in 2022). It is less than 6 paise per day for ₹2,00,000 insurance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between PMJJBY and PMSBY?
faqs.a: PMJJBY costs ₹436/year and covers death due to ANY reason (illness, heart attack, cancer, or accident). PMSBY costs ₹20/year and covers ONLY accidental death and permanent accidental disability.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for PMSBY?
faqs.a: You can join PMSBY between 18 and 70 years of age (compared to 50 for PMJJBY).

faqs.q: Does PMSBY cover permanent disability like loss of sight or limb?
faqs.a: Yes! Total irreversible loss of both eyes, hands, or feet receives ₹2,00,000; loss of one eye, hand, or foot receives ₹1,00,000.

faqs.q: Can both husband and wife enroll in PMSBY?
faqs.a: Yes. Both husband and wife can hold separate PMSBY policies in their individual bank accounts for ₹20 each.

faqs.q: What should the nominee do in case of accidental death?
faqs.a: Within 30 days of the accident, the nominee should take the death certificate, FIR copy, post-mortem report, and bank passbook to the deceased's bank branch to submit the claim.

process: Step 1: Obtain the NSAP Old Age Pension application form from your local Gram Panchayat Secretary, BDO office, or Municipal Corporation.
Step 2: Fill in personal details, age, BPL household ID, and Aadhaar number.
Step 3: Attach verified copies of: Age Proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID), BPL Ration Card, and Bank Passbook.
Step 4: Submit to the Gram Panchayat Secretary (rural) or Municipal Ward Officer (urban).
Step 5: Village level social welfare committee / Panchayat verifies BPL status and age.
Step 6: Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Taluk Social Welfare Officer sanctions the pension order.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to receive IGNOAPS?
faqs.a: The applicant must be 60 years of age or older.

faqs.q: What is the difference in pension between age 60 and age 80?
faqs.a: Beneficiaries aged 60 to 79 receive the base central contribution of ₹200 (plus state top-up). Upon turning 80, the central contribution increases to ₹500 (plus state top-up).

faqs.q: How much pension is paid in total each month?
faqs.a: Most state governments add a substantial top-up (e.g. ₹1,000 in UP, ₹1,200 in Karnataka, ₹1,500 in Maharashtra, ₹2,000 in Telangana/AP), making the total monthly payment ₹1,000 to ₹2,500+.

faqs.q: How can elderly citizens submit their annual life certificate?
faqs.a: You can submit a Digital Life Certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) using facial authentication on an Android phone, through an India Post postman at your doorstep, or in person at your bank branch.

faqs.q: Can both husband and wife aged 60+ receive this pension?
faqs.a: Yes! If both husband and wife are aged 60 or above and belong to a BPL household, both can receive individual monthly pensions in their respective bank accounts.

faqs.q: What happens if a beneficiary's fingerprints are worn out?
faqs.a: Life certificate submission supports Iris scan and Face Authentication on Android smartphones, eliminating fingerprint failure issues.

faqs.q: What is the minimum disability percentage required for IGNDPS?
faqs.a: Under Central NSAP guidelines, the applicant must have 80% or higher disability (severe disability) or multiple disabilities. However, several state governments have their own state schemes that cover persons with 40% to 79% disability.

faqs.q: How much pension will I actually receive?
faqs.a: While the central contribution is ₹300, most state governments contribute a significant top-up, resulting in total monthly payments ranging between ₹1,000 and ₹3,000+ depending on your state.

faqs.q: What happens when a beneficiary turns 80 years old?
faqs.a: Upon attaining 80 years of age, the beneficiary is automatically migrated to the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) at the higher senior citizen rate.

faqs.q: Can a disabled person receive this pension if they live with their parents?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the household is categorized as Below Poverty Line (BPL).

faqs.q: How do I submit my annual Life Certificate?
faqs.a: You can submit a digital life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) using facial authentication on an Android phone, at any CSC, or in person at your bank branch/Panchayat.

faqs.q: Can the pension be delivered at home if the person is bedridden?
faqs.a: Yes, in many states, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) postmen provide Doorstep Banking (AePS) to deliver cash directly to bedridden beneficiaries at home.
