process: Step 1: Visit the official portal swavlambancard.gov.in and click 'Apply for Disability Certificate & UDID Card'.
Step 2: Enter Personal Details (Name, Father's Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Mobile Number, Category).
Step 3: Enter Address for correspondence and upload Aadhaar card as address proof.
Step 4: Enter Disability Details: Choose disability type from the 21 listed categories, hospital where assessed, and whether you hold an existing certificate.
Step 5: Upload your passport photo and signature/thumb impression.
Step 6: Submit application. An Enrolment Number / Application ID is generated.
Step 7: The portal assigns your application to your District Hospital / CMO Medical Board.
Step 8: Visit the District Hospital on the scheduled medical board day for physical examination.
Step 9: Medical Board assesses disability percentage and inputs findings into the portal.
Step 10: CMO digitally signs the certificate. Download the digital e-UDID card immediately, and the laminated plastic Smart Card is dispatched to your postal address via India Post.

faqs.q: Is the UDID card valid in all states across India?
faqs.a: Yes. The UDID card is a national document issued by the Central Government and is recognized across all states, union territories, Indian Railways, and state transport undertakings.

faqs.q: How many disabilities are covered under the UDID scheme?
faqs.a: All 21 disabilities specified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016 are covered, including locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment, mental illness, autism, intellectual disability, and chronic neurological conditions.

faqs.q: Does the UDID card cost any money?
faqs.a: No. The UDID application, medical board assessment at government hospitals, and delivery of the plastic card are 100% free.

faqs.q: Can I get railway travel concessions with a UDID card?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian Railways has integrated the UDID number into its e-ticketing system, allowing online booking of concessional tickets on IRCTC without visiting railway counters.

faqs.q: What should I do if my physical card is lost?
faqs.a: You can download the digital e-UDID card anytime from swavlambancard.gov.in or apply for a duplicate replacement card on the portal.

faqs.q: Can an existing state disability certificate holder apply?
faqs.a: Yes. While applying, select 'Have Disability Certificate', enter your old certificate details, and upload a copy. The medical board will verify and convert it to a national UDID.

financialBenefit: Universal single identity card unlocking rail/bus fare concessions (up to 75%), monthly disability pensions, and free aids & appliances
benefitFrequency: Permanent smart card (or valid for specified medical renewal period)

Step 2: If not in the survey, apply for a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from your local Urban Local Body / Municipality.
Step 3: Click 'Apply for Loan' and enter your Aadhaar-linked Mobile Number.
Step 4: Enter the 12-digit Aadhaar number and verify via Aadhaar OTP.
Step 5: Verify your Vendor Details (Vending category, Vending location/ward, and Average daily sales).
Step 6: Enter your Bank Account details and select your preferred lending bank branch.
Step 7: Choose your loan tranche (1st Loan: ₹10,000).
Step 8: Submit the application. Your Application ID is generated.
Step 9: Selected bank branch processes the application; no physical branch visit or collateral is needed.
Step 10: Loan amount (₹10,000) is credited directly into your bank account within 7 to 10 days.

faqs.q: Is collateral or security required for a PM SVANidhi loan?
faqs.a: No! All loans under PM SVANidhi are 100% collateral-free. You do not need to pledge any property, gold, or third-party guarantee.

faqs.q: How much interest subsidy does the vendor receive?
faqs.a: Vendors who repay their monthly installments on time receive a 7% interest subsidy per annum credited directly into their bank account on a quarterly basis.

faqs.q: How do I qualify for the 2nd loan of ₹20,000 and 3rd loan of ₹50,000?
faqs.a: Simply repay your 1st loan of ₹10,000 in monthly installments on or before the due date. Once fully repaid, the portal automatically unlocks your 2nd tranche of ₹20,000. Repaying the 2nd tranche unlocks ₹50,000.

faqs.q: What is the digital transaction cashback?
faqs.a: If you accept payments through any UPI QR code (PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm, BHIM), the government credits up to ₹100 per month (total ₹1,200 per year) as direct cashback into your bank account.

faqs.q: What if my name is not in the street vendor survey?
faqs.a: You can apply for a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from your local municipality or Urban Local Body, which grants immediate eligibility for the loan.

faqs.q: Can vegetable and fruit vendors in rural village markets apply?
faqs.a: The scheme covers vendors operating in urban local bodies and peri-urban areas surrounding cities and towns.

financialBenefit: Collateral-free working capital loan up to ₹50,000 (₹10K -> ₹20K -> ₹50K) + 7% interest subsidy + ₹1,200 annual digital cashback
benefitFrequency: Term micro-credit tranches with monthly installments
impact: Liberates millions of street vendors from high-interest informal moneylenders charging 5% to 10% daily interest, creates digital credit scores, and integrates street vendors into formal retail banking.

department: Ministry of Rural Development
applyChannel: your Gram Panchayat
description: Legal guarantee of wage employment for rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
whoCanApply: Adult members of any rural household willing to do unskilled manual work.
benefits: Statutory guarantee of 100 days of wage employment per rural household per financial year (extended to 150 days in notified drought-hit blocks). Daily wage rate is notified annually by the Central Government (ranging from ₹234 to ₹374 per day depending on state). If work is not provided within 15 days of application, the government is legally mandated to pay an Unemployment Allowance directly to the worker.

process: Step 1: Submit an application for a Job Card (written or oral) to your Gram Panchayat Secretary or Rozgar Sevak.
Step 2: Provide names, age, Aadhaar, and photos of all adult household members willing to work.
Step 3: Gram Panchayat verifies local residency and issues your free MGNREGA Job Card within 15 days.
Step 4: Submit an application for work (Form 6) to the Gram Panchayat, specifying dates and duration of work requested.
Step 5: Gram Panchayat issues a dated receipt acknowledging your demand for work.
Step 6: Within 15 days, the Panchayat assigns work at a local asset project (pond digging, check dam, canal lining, plantation).
Step 7: Report to worksite. Work attendance is marked twice daily using the National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) app.
Step 8: Measurement of work done is recorded in the measurement book by the Technical Assistant.
Step 9: Wage list is electronically generated on NREGASoft.
Step 10: Wages are credited directly into your Aadhaar-seeded bank account within 15 days of work completion.

faqs.q: What is the unemployment allowance under MGNREGA?
faqs.a: By law, if the Gram Panchayat fails to provide employment within 15 days of receiving your work application, the state government MUST pay an Unemployment Allowance directly into your bank account (at least 1/4th of wage rate for first 30 days, and 1/2 of wage rate thereafter).

faqs.q: What is the daily wage rate under MGNREGA?
faqs.a: Wages are revised every year by the Ministry of Rural Development and vary by state (e.g. ₹234 in UP/Bihar, ₹316 in Karnataka, ₹374 in Haryana).

faqs.q: Can women do MGNREGA work?
faqs.a: Yes! Over 57% of all MGNREGA workers across India are women. The law mandates equal wages for men and women, and crèche facilities must be provided at worksites where 5+ children are present.

faqs.q: Is the Job Card issued for an individual or a family?
faqs.a: The Job Card is issued to the entire household, and all adult members of the family are listed with their photographs in the same booklet.

faqs.q: How many days of work can one family get in a year?
faqs.a: A rural household is entitled to a minimum of 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per financial year (April to March).

faqs.q: What work facilities must be provided at the worksite?
faqs.a: Safe drinking water, shade for resting, a first-aid medical kit, and crèche facilities for small children must be provided free of cost at every worksite.

purpose: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, is a statutory rights-based employment guarantee that enhances livelihood security in rural India by legally guaranteeing at least 100 days of wage employment in every financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
targetBeneficiary: Adult members of rural households willing to do unskilled manual work at notified statutory wages.

benefitFrequency: Weekly / fortnightly direct bank transfer into worker's account
impact: World's largest public works employment safety net, prevents distress rural-to-urban migration, raises agricultural baseline wages, builds durable rural water-harvesting assets and rural roads, and ensures gender wage parity (over 57% women workers).

process: Step 1: As soon as pregnancy is detected, register with your local Anganwadi Worker (AWW) or ASHA to receive your MCP Card.
Step 2: Visit pmmvy.wcd.gov.in and click 'Citizen Login'.
Step 3: Register using your Mobile Number and verify via OTP.
Step 4: Select 'Data Entry' -> 'Beneficiary Registration'.
Step 5: Fill in Mother's Name, Aadhaar, LMP date, MCP Card number, and Husband's Aadhaar.
Step 6: Select your qualifying vulnerability category and upload the document.
Step 7: Provide Mother's Aadhaar-seeded bank account details.
Step 8: Submit Form 1A. First installment of ₹3,000 is credited following ANC verification.
Step 9: After child delivery, log in to claim Form 1B: enter child's birth certificate and vaccination records.
Step 10: Second installment of ₹2,000 (or ₹6,000 if 2nd girl child) is credited via PFMS.

faqs.q: Can I receive benefits for a second child under PMMVY?
faqs.a: Under PMMVY 2.0, a mother receives a special enhanced benefit of ₹6,000 in a single installment for a second child, provided the baby born is a girl child.

faqs.q: Can PMMVY and JSY benefits be taken together?
faqs.a: Yes! A woman delivering her first child in a government hospital receives ₹5,000 from PMMVY PLUS ₹1,400 from JSY, making total cash assistance ₹6,400.

faqs.q: What if a woman conceives before 19 years of age?
faqs.a: To discourage early teenage pregnancies, the scheme strictly mandates that the mother must be 19 years or older at conception.

faqs.q: Do I need an income certificate to apply?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Any 1 of 11 proofs (e-Shram card, MGNREGA job card, PM-JAY card, BPL card, SC/ST certificate, or income certificate < ₹8 Lakh) is accepted.

faqs.q: What should I do if my first installment has not arrived?
faqs.a: Check your Aadhaar seeding status with your bank and inquire with your local Child Development Project Officer (CDPO).

faqs.q: Is the benefit paid if the child is stillborn?
faqs.a: If an eligible mother receives the 1st installment but experiences a stillbirth, she remains eligible for the 2nd installment upon a subsequent pregnancy.

benefitFrequency: Instalment-based milestone disbursement per pregnancy
impact: Compensates wage loss, guarantees essential maternal nutrition during crucial gestational trimesters, and promotes survival and care of infant daughters.

department: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance

description: Government-backed small savings scheme for the education and marriage expenses of a girl child.
whoCanApply: Parents or legal guardians of a girl child below 10 years of age (up to two girls per family, with exceptions for twins).

Complete 'EEE' (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) tax benefit under Section 80C. Up to 50% withdrawal permitted for higher education once the girl turns 18, and full maturity corpus with compound interest handed over when the account matures after 21 years.

process: Step 1: Visit any Post Office branch or authorized commercial bank (SBI, PNB, BoB, Canara, HDFC, ICICI, etc.).
Step 2: Collect and fill out the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Opening Form (Form-1).
Step 3: Provide girl child's details (Name, Date of Birth, Birth Certificate Number).
Step 4: Provide parent/guardian KYC details (Aadhaar, PAN, residential address).
Step 5: Attach verified copies of child's Birth Certificate and guardian's KYC documents.
Step 6: Pay the initial opening deposit (minimum ₹250) in cash, cheque, or demand draft.
Step 7: The post office/bank generates the SSY account and issues a dedicated passbook.
Step 8: Deposit funds anytime (minimum ₹250, maximum ₹1,50,000 per year) via cash, cheque, or net banking / IPPB app.
Step 9: Continue deposits for 15 years from account opening date.
Step 10: At age 18, withdraw up to 50% for college fees, or withdraw the entire matured amount tax-free after 21 years.

faqs.q: What is the current interest rate on Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana?
faqs.a: The Government of India offers an attractive 8.2% annual compound interest rate (reviewed quarterly by the Ministry of Finance).

faqs.q: For how many years do I need to deposit money?
faqs.a: Deposits must be made for 15 years from the date of account opening. The account continues to earn interest until maturity (21 years from opening) even without fresh deposits from years 16 to 21.

faqs.q: Can I withdraw money before 21 years?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the girl child turns 18 years old or passes Class 10, partial withdrawal up to 50% of the account balance is permitted specifically for higher education admission fees.

faqs.q: Is the maturity amount taxable?
faqs.a: No! Sukanya Samriddhi has 'EEE' (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) status. The annual deposit qualifies for Section 80C rebate, the interest earned is 100% tax-free, and the final maturity amount is completely exempt from income tax.

faqs.q: Can I transfer the account if I relocate to another city?
faqs.a: Yes. SSY accounts can be transferred free of charge anywhere in India from one Post Office to another, or between post offices and banks.

faqs.q: What happens if the girl gets married before 21 years?
faqs.a: The account can be closed early upon marriage, provided the girl has attained 18 years of age at the time of marriage.

benefitFrequency: Flexible annual deposits (Minimum ₹250 to Maximum ₹1,50,000 per financial year) for 15 years

faqs.q: Is Gruha Lakshmi only for BPL families?
faqs.a: No! Gruha Lakshmi covers BPL, Antyodaya (AAY), AND APL (Above Poverty Line) cardholders, provided the woman and her husband are not income tax or GST payers.

faqs.q: What should I do if my application was approved but no money came?
faqs.a: Download the 'Karnataka DBT' mobile app, log in with your Aadhaar, and check the reason. Over 95% of payment failures are due to the bank account not being seeded with Aadhaar on the NPCI server.

faqs.q: Can an unmarried or single woman receive Gruha Lakshmi?
faqs.a: Yes, if an unmarried, widowed, or divorced woman is listed as the head of the household on her ration card, she is fully eligible.

faqs.q: How much fee is charged at Grama One for registration?
faqs.a: Registration for Gruha Lakshmi at Grama One, Karnataka One, and Bangalore One is completely FREE. No operator can charge any fee.

faqs.q: Can a family receive both Gruha Lakshmi and Anna Bhagya?
faqs.a: Yes! Gruha Lakshmi (₹2,000/month) and Anna Bhagya (free rice/DBT cash for food) are complementary guarantee schemes and families can receive both.

faqs.q: Can I receive the money in a post office account?
faqs.a: Yes! India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) accounts with Aadhaar seeding are fully supported and often provide faster DBT credits.

purpose: Gruha Lakshmi is the flagship gender equity initiative of the Government of Karnataka, guaranteeing direct monthly financial autonomy of ₹2,000 to the woman head of household in every eligible family in Karnataka, recognizing unpaid domestic labor and shielding families from inflation.
targetBeneficiary: Woman head of household listed on Antyodaya (AAY), Priority Household (BPL), or Non-Priority Household (APL) ration cards in Karnataka.
financialBenefit: ₹2,000 per month (₹24,000 per year) directly credited via DBT
benefitFrequency: Monthly direct bank transfer
impact: Provides financial independence to over 1.15 crore women in Karnataka, supports household nutrition, children's school expenses, and emergency medical savings.
